documents.title: Doc 97 - DECISION - Car 15 - alleged yellow flag violation
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 15 - alleged yellow flag violation

details.fact: Car 15 (Dunne) was alleged to have breached yellow flag regulations at Turn 16 (mini sectors 16 and 17) on Lap 9.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L Chapter IV, Article 1 and Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 93) and heard the Driver of Car 15 (Dunne) and the team representative. They examined video and telemetry evidence. The driver of Car 15 was reported as potentially not respecting the yellow flag that was present in sectors 16 and 17. Sector 16 starts at the exit of Turn 15 and ends at the entrance to T16 where sector 17 begins and then ends at the entrance to Turn 17. Car 21 was ahead of Car 15 entering T15 and was the first car to be shown the yellow flag. Car 15 is the second car to be shown the yellow flag that is clearly visible from the drivers onboard camera at both panels 16 and 17. Panel 18 is green. On the lap in question car 15 is on his 3rd lap of new tyres having pitted at the end of lap 6. His sector times are some of the quickest prior to this point on this lap and it appears that his tyres have reached their peak performance. The sector times reveal that Car 15 does his fastest time through sector 16 and is then is 0.093 slower than his fastest sector in sector 17. At the hearing the driver reported that he had seen the yellow flags. that he had braked earlier and did not accelerate to full throttle until he was clear of the area and could see the green flag. The Technical Delegate provided the telemetry from Car 15 and confirmed that the driver braked 50 meters earlier into T16 and accelerated more than 50 meters later out of T16. This clearly demonstrates compliance with the regulations. Accordingly the Stewards take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 55 - DECISION - Car 5 - allegedly impeded Car 17
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 5 - allegedly impeded Car 17

details.fact: Car 5 (Leon) allegedly impeded Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) from Turn 2 in Qualifying 1.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: After the session, the Race Director reported a potential impeding incident involving Cars 5 and 17. The Stewards summoned (Documents 35 & 36) and heard the Drivers of Car 5 (Leon) and Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) and the team representatives. They examined video, GPS and timing evidence. Car 17 was running behind Car 5 when both cars began a push lap. As they approached Turn 1, Cars 15 and 9 positioned ahead of Car 5 left the track, resulting in Car 5 effectively leading the pack through the subsequent corners. From that point onward, Car 17 steadily reduced the gap to Car 5, bringing it down to approximately one second by the approach to Turn 4. Both drivers continued pushing throughout the lap, with the driver of Car 17 opting to stay behind the car in front. At no point did Car 17 show a clear intention to overtake, and based on the available evidence, a pass was not achievable. The data showed that the driver of Car 5 achieved 2 of his fastest sectors in the early part of the lap but then he progressively lost time although still on a push lap. When assessing a potential impeding situation, the Stewards consider whether a driver has been unnecessarily impeded and whether the driver was affected. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the driver of Car 17 was affected but was not unnecessarily impeded by the driver of Car 5. Accordingly, no further action will be taken on this occasion.

documents.title: Doc 54 - DECISION - Car 14 - allegedly impeded Car 17
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 14 - allegedly impeded Car 17

details.fact: Car 14 (Stenshorne) allegedly impeded Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) between Turn 18-19 in Qualifying 1.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 33 & 34) and heard the Drivers of Car 14 (Stenshorne) and Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) and the team representatives. They examined video and GPS evidence. Car 14 and Car 17 were preparing to start a push lap and this is done from the exit of Turn 16 on the preceding lap. Car 17 was behind Car 14 with an approximate 1 second gap. Video evidence showed that Car 17 had closed the gap to Car 14 by Turn 19 and given that he had the benefit of a tow he had to slow. Car 17 then passed Car 14 and started his push lap. Car 14 abandoned the lap and entered the pit lane. The driver of Car 14 reported that he intended to start a push lap but when he saw that Car 17 had benefited from the tow and that he would likely be passed or would have to fight into Turn 1 he abandoned the lap. The driver of Car 17 reported that the preparation for a push lap starts at the exit of T16 and he expected Car 14 to be at full speed through T19 and T20 and he was surprised that Car 14 stayed on the line and appeared not to be at full speed. As a result of not having a tow on the main straight leading to the start of the push lap Car 17 was 10 kph slower than he had been on previous laps when he had a car in front to give a tow. The only sector that could be affected by the interaction of Cars 14 and 17 on the push lap that started was Sector 1. In that sector Car 17 was 0.11 seconds slower than his fastest sector time which was achieved when he had the benefit of the tow. There is no doubt that Car 17 was affected by Car 14 who was not as fast through Turns 18 and 19 but that of itself is not evidence of unnecessary impeding. In fact Car 17 may have benefited from a tow from Car 14 up until Car 14 moved to the left to enter the pit lane. The Stewards therefore conclude that there is no evidence of unnecessary impeding and take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 53 - DECISION - Qualifying 1 - allegedly driving unnecessarily slowly
documents.subject: DECISION - Qualifying 1 - allegedly driving unnecessarily slowly

details.fact: The drivers listed below were allegedly driving unnecessarily slowly between Turn 4 and Turn 7.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The stewards received a report from the Race Director that Cars #7, 9, 6, 14, 20, 5, 3, 2, 15, 16, 24, 17 were driving unnecessarily slowly between Turns 4 and 7. After reviewing the video and telemetry the Stewards could see that all 12 cars involved were on the same sequence having just completed a push lap and were now on a cool down lap. Car 7 (the first car) slowed progressively without any sudden braking or change of direction and at all times remained off the racing line. As each driver behind caught up to Car 7 they also slowed and stayed in line without affecting any other driver. Eventually there was a line of 12 cars and at the exit of Turn 6 the entire pack of cars slowed to approximately 30 kph. BAKU EVENT 23 TO 26 SEPTEMBER 2026 The Stewards summoned and heard the drivers listed above and their team representatives, as well as the driver of Car 7 (Beganovic) and his team representative (Documents 37 to 48). The drivers each reported that they were aware that the following cars were all on the same sequence and were trying to stay in the order without passing They further reported that in their experience it is safer to stay in the sequence rather than pull out into the racing line and potentially end up impeding a following driver or driving side by side with another car. Eventually one of the cars at the rear of the pack did pull out and passed the line and the whole group accelerated without issue to Turns 7 and 8. Having considered the matter extensively and with special attention to recent similar incidents in this season the Stewards found that the conditions in this case were material different as there was no erratic driving, unusual braking and there did not appear to be any dangerous situation created. However, the driver of car 7 did not need to slow to this level and still considered that the slow speed was unnecessary and in a separate decision issued a penalty. For the remaining drivers the Stewards elect to take no further action.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 e of the FIA International Sporting Code.

documents.title: Doc 22 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - overtook Car 3 under yellow flag conditions
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - overtook Car 3 under yellow flag conditions

details.fact: Car 20 (Fittipaldi) overtook Car 3 (Miyata) under single yellow conditions between Turn 2 and Turn 3.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 20. This is his first Driving Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 14 & 16) and heard the Drivers of Car 20 (Fittipaldi) and Car 3 (Miyata) and the team representatives. They examined video and GPS evidence. A car was stationary on track in T3 and this caused a single yellow to be displayed at panels 4 and 5. Panel 4 is at the exit of Turn 2 on the outside. Car 3 was on a cool down lap and was aware that Car 20 was on a push lap and approaching at high speed into Turn 2. Car 3 moved to the left off the racing line after exiting Turn 2. The driver of Car 20 explained that he was on a push lap and saw Car 3 ahead and was expecting to pass him after exiting Turn 2. He further explained that at the exit he saw Car 3 move to the left and he concentrated on avoiding him and still managing the exit of Turn 2. He noticed the panel ahead (panel 5) and immediately reduced speed. However, he admitted that by then he had passed Car 3 within the yellow flag sector which he had not seen. The Stewards find that Car 20 overtook Car 3 after passing Panel 4 while it was displaying a single-yellow signal. The driver’s failure to notice that signal does not remove the obligation to comply with it, and the Stewards therefore find a breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5(b). In determining the penalty, the Stewards took into account the relative speeds of the cars, Car 3’s movement off the racing line at the exit of Turn 2, the interaction between the cars at the start of the yellow-flag sector, and Car 20’s immediate reduction in speed upon observing Panel 5. Having considered the penalty recommended in the Penalty Guidelines for failing to slow under a single yellow as a comparator, the Stewards determine that a Driving Reprimand is proportionate to the particular circumstances of this overtaking infringement.

documents.title: Doc 51 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - off track and gained lasting advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - off track and gained lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 6 (Tsolov) went off track while passing Car 9 (Mini) and gained lasting advantage.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Five seconds (5) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (a) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 48 & 49) and heard the Drivers of Car 6 (Tsolov) and Car 9 (Mini) and the team representatives. The Stewards, together with the Drivers and Team Representatives, reviewed video evidence including CCTV and drone footage, TV host high resolution images and Cars’ 6, 9, and 15 onboard cameras. The Driver of Car 6 explained that he was on soft tyres and he attacked Car 9 at the breaking point of Turn 10, where Car 9 ran wide. Due to the different tyre strategy, it was a simple move at the exit of Turn 10 and entry of Turn 11. He stated that he did not leave the track and that the move was already completed. The Driver Car 9 explained that he was defending the position, and that he exited turn 10 quite tight leaving a lot of room at the inside of Turn 11 for Car 6. He also stated that Car 6 left the track and gained a lasting advantage by completing the manoeuvre off track. Having considered that matter extensively the Stewards determined that Car 6 left the track at Turn 11 and completed an overtaking move by exceeding the track limits. The Stewards find that mitigating circumstances exist to impose a 5 second time penalty on this occasion rather than the usual penalty of 10 seconds. The mitigating circumstances are that Car 6 left the track at Turn 11 for a extremely short period of time, video evidence also confirmed that despite Car 6 being off track, the distance to the white line was marginal, to the extent that the Stewards’ needed the TV host high resolution images to determine that an infringement was committed.

documents.title: Doc 39 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 22 - left the track and gained lasting advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 22 - left the track and gained lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 22 (Varrone) left the track at Turn 1 and gained lasting advantage over Car 11 (Montoya).
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Five seconds (5) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (a) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 31 & 32) and heard the Drivers of Car 22 (Varrone) and Car 11 (Montoya) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence and onboard footage. During the hearing the Driver of Car 11 stated that he was ahead at the apex and he had the right of the corner. He also stated that at the apex, Car 22 moved slightly to the right, forcing him slightly to the kerb, which caused his car to snap, and contact with Car 22. That circumstance was confirmed by his team representative who added that the cars were alongside at the apex and it was not a dive in manoeuvre. The Driver of Car 22 stated that he was defending the position and he received a small contact due to a snap from Car 11 and, for that reason, Car 22 had to go off track and followed the escape road. The team representative of Car 22 also stated that his driver in this position could not have disappeared and it was the reason why he had to leave the track. The Stewards determined that the Drivers of Car 22 and Car 11 were fighting for position at Turn 1. Car 11 made an attempt to overtake and at the apex of Turn 1 was ahead of Car 22 that was defending the position. During the manoeuvre, Car 11 had a slight touch with Car 22 who at that moment lost the right of the turn. For the contact the Stewards found that no drivers were wholly or predominately to blame. However after the small contact, Car 22 went out of the track by using the escape road and in doing so gained the position on Car 11 when he rejoined the track. On this occasion, the Stewards consider that if a car defending the position leaves the track and re-joins in the same position, it has to be considered as having gained a lasting advantage. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards noted that in this specific case despite Car 22 trying to give some of the advantage back, the driver was unable to do it fully as Car 14 had overtaken Car 11. Therefore, the Stewards elected to assess a lower penalty than the baseline for such an offence.

documents.title: Doc 24 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 2 - failed to respect yellow flags in Qualifying
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 2 - failed to respect yellow flags in Qualifying

details.fact: Car 2 (Durksen) failed to respect the yellow flag requirements at Turn 14 in Qualifying, where Car 3 (Miyata) had crashed.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L Chapter IV, Article 1 and Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A drop of 5 places on the grid for the Sprint Race & Feature Race at this Competition, as per Article 31.5 of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 5 points
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 19) and heard the Driver of Car 2 (Durksen) and the team representative. The FIA F2 Technical Delegate and the F2 Technical Director were also present during the hearing. The Stewards examined GPS, car data, marshalling sector times and video evidence. The Driver of Car 2 explained that as soon as he finished the corner (Turn 14), he received the yellow flag and saw Car 3 (Miyata) in the wall. He stated that he was under control of the situation, and considered it safe, as Car 3 was far away from the track. The team representative stated that there was a short time from the yellow flag until the end of the lap, therefore Car 2 did not have sufficient time to react to the flag. Video evidence shows marshal post 16.6 waving a single yellow flag while Car 2 is exiting Turn 14. The marshalling sector chart showed that in mini sector 16, which covered the single yellow flag area, the driver set his fastest sector time of the session. Having considered the matter extensively, Stewards determined that Car 2 failed to reduce the speed under a single yellow flag condition. Car data confirmed that Car 2 didn’t brake earlier and/or noticeably reduce the speed in that sector as required by Appendix H Article 2.5.5 b) of the FIA International Sporting Code. Therefore, Stewards decide to impose the standard penalty of a drop of 5 grid positions for both Sprint and Feature race plus 2 penalty points.

documents.title: DOC 45 - 2026 Budapest Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - left the track and gained lasting advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - left the track and gained lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 4 (Herta) cut the chicane at Turn 7 and gained lasting advantage over Car 15 (Dunne).
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Approaching Turn 6 Car 15 attempted an inside pass on Car 4. Car 15 was alongside prior to and at the apex of Turn 6, then Car 4 went wide and off the track and rejoined after Turn 7 ahead of Car 15. To have the rights for a turn the car who is trying to overtake on the inside has to have its front axle at least alongside the mirror of the other car prior to and at the apex, and in this case Car 15 earned the rights for the turn. The Stewards considered that Car 4 went off track at Turn 7 and after rejoining the track gained a position over Car 15. The Stewards, having analysed extensively the matter, under these circumstances considered that failing to lose an advantage constitutes gaining an advantage. Therefore the Stewards elect to impose the standard penalty for leaving the track and gaining a lasting advantage.

documents.title: Doc 56 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - leaving the track and gaining lasting advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - leaving the track and gaining lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 5 (Leon) went off track at Turn 5 and gained lasting advantage over Car 24 (Van Hoepen).
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 5 (Leon). This is his first Driving Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 50 & 51) and heard the Drivers of Car 5 (Leon) and Car 24 (Van Hoepen) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence. Car 24 made a pass on Car 5 going into Turn 5. Car 5 left the track, followed the RD instructions and took the correct path around the bollard but rejoined ahead of Car 24 thereby gaining a position off track. After approximately 2.5 laps Car 5 gave back the position. At the hearing the driver of Car 5 explained that while he knew that he was passed on the inside of Turn 5 by Car 24 he was not sure if Car 24 had fully made the corner nor followed the RD instructions and as such was not sure if Car 24 was entitled to the position. He reported that he immediately asked his team to verify if Car 24 had made the corner and if so he would give back the position. The team had to wait for a replay to verify if the driver of Car 24 had in fact stayed on track. As soon as the team reported to him that Car 24 had remained on track he conceded the position. The Stewards also noted that Car 24 confirmed that the position had been fully restored and raised no further issue concerning the manner in which it was conceded. Although the position was ultimately conceded, the Stewards considered that retaining it for approximately 2.5 laps constituted a lasting advantage within the meaning of Article 27.3. The drivers have been trained that whenever they consider that they have gained a position off track they are to give back the position as soon as possible and at the latest within 1 lap. If in doubt it is always better to give up a position than to get a penalty after investigation. In this case the driver of Car 5 was fortunate that the position was still available to be given back after the lengthy delay of 2.5 laps. Given the unique circumstances in this case, and considering that the driver of Car 5 had immediately queried the status of Car 24 specifically if he had remained on track, the Stewards consider this significant mitigating circumstances that warrants a lesser penalty than the standard 10 seconds and gave a Driving Reprimand.

documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 11 - released in an unsafe condition

details.fact: The Competitor released Car 11 (Montoya) whilst it was in an unsafe condition.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 28.12 (b) of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A fine of 1000 Euros to be paid by the Competitor. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 20) and heard the team representative. They examined the photograph presented by the Technical Delegate, and reviewed video evidence. During the Qualifying session, Car 11 impacted the wall in Turn 11 and sustained damage to the right rear suspension. The driver returned to the pit lane and the mechanics attempted to repair the damage. The lower wish bone was noticed to be severely bent to the point that in one section it was visibly “kinked”. A member of the technical delegate's team took a photograph of the component. The team mechanics for Car 11 made a decision that the car was safe to return to the track and instructed the driver to follow an installation lap protocol with the expectation that they would further evaluate the car upon its return to the pit lane. During this lap the driver reported that “he lost drive” and he returned to the pit lane and retired the car. The Technical Delegate reported to the Stewards that in his opinion the lower wish bone suspension component was damaged to a degree that it was unsafe to release the car to the track. Having heard from both the team representative and the Technical Delegate and having reviewed the photographic evidence. the Stewards concluded that the car was released in an unsafe condition because of the established suspension damage.

documents.title: Doc 45 - DECISION - Car 22 - alleged pit lane incident with Car 21 in Race 1
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 22 - alleged pit lane incident with Car 21 in Race 1

details.fact: Incident between Car 22 (Varrone) in the fast lane and Car 21 (Shields) waiting to depart his pit box.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 40 & 41) and heard the Drivers of Car 22 (Varrone) and Car 21 (Shields) and the team representatives. The Stewards reviewed the available evidence, including video footage from the pit lane cameras. During the Safety Car period, Car 22 entered the pit lane to perform a tyre change. The team of Car 22 was conducting a double-stacked pit stop. When Car 22 was approaching its pit position, its team-mate was still stationary due to a problem during the pit stop and could therefore not be released in time. At the same time, Car 21, which was pitted in the pit position behind Car 22, was ready to be released. However, the team of Car 21 acted conservatively and delayed the release of Car 21 in order to avoid a potential unsafe release into the fast lane with Car 22. As the driver of Car 22 did not want to stop in the fast lane, he proceeded forward in the pit lane and moved ahead of Car 21. Only after Car 22 had cleared the area was Car 21 able to leave its pit position. The Stewards acknowledge that Car 21 was impeded as a result of this situation. However, having considered the circumstances, the Stewards determined that Car 22 did not stop in the fast lane and did not perform any manoeuvre considered dangerous or in breach of the pit lane regulations. The situation arose as a consequence of the delayed release of Car 22’s team-mate during the double-stack pit stop and the cautious release decision taken by the team of Car 21. Accordingly, the Stewards find no breach of the Regulations and therefore take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 44 - DECISION - Car 4 - incident involving Car 6 in Race 1
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 4 - incident involving Car 6 in Race 1

details.fact: Incident between Car 4 (Herta) and Car 6 (Tsolov) at Turn 5.

details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 38 & 39) and heard the Drivers of Car 6 (Tsolov) and Car 4 (Herta) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence. Car 6 was passed by another car on the run from T1 to T3. Car 4 was behind Car 6 at T3. Car 6 chose to exit T3 leaving room on the outside for Car 4. Car 4 then made a passing attempt on the inside of T4 and had gained rights per the DSGs. Car 6 appeared at first to be aware of Car 4 and was leaving room but at the apex he squeezed Car 4 unto the curb causing car 4 to understeer. Car 6 still had more room on the outside of T4 but by squeezing Car 4 there was contact. Both drivers contributed in some measure to the incident although Car 6 moreso. Car 6 spun as a result of the contact and Car 4 continued. Based on the entire circumstances, the Stewards determine that neither driver was wholly nor predominately at fault and hence take no further action.

details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 28.12 (a) of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 58 and 59) and heard the Driver and team representative of Car 3 and Car 12 and reviewed video evidence. The driver of car 24 reported that he left his pit position as soon as he was signaled to do so. He said he saw that there were no cars in the fast lane behind. He said that he had some wheel spin from the wet conditions but upon entering the fast lane he saw that car 22 was now fully in the fast lane, and decided that it was safer to continue than to brake. The driver of car 22 reported that he saw car 24 entering ahead and had to lift and tap his brakes a little. It appeared that both drivers acted appropriately and no rule was breached.

documents.title: Doc 71 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - Safety car infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - Safety car infringement

details.fact: Crossed the white line at pit entry.
details.infringement: Breach of ISC Apdx L Chap IV (d)
details.decision: Warning to driver
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 54). At the start of the race Lap 1 Turn 1 an incident occurred necessitating the deployment of the Safety Car. As the leaders were approaching T17 the Race Director notified the teams that the drivers should follow Safety Car through the pit lane. Panels 19 and 20 were illuminated with a yellow arrow pointing to the right. The RD used this signal per Art 40.11 with the intention of notifying the drivers to enter the pit lane. The leader was approximately 50 meters before panel 19 when it was illuminated. The track condition was very wet and there was significant spray reducing visibility although it appeared from the drivers onboard camera that the panels were visible. There is no way for the Stewards to know when the drivers were notified by radio of the RD’s instruction to enter the pit lane. Some teams may react quicker than others and it is impossible to know what other radio traffic may affect how quickly the message can be delivered to individual drivers. The light panel signal showing a red arrow on a yellow background is used to indicate to a driver the side of the track that they should chose because of an issue in the area. It is not an exclusive instruction to enter the pit lane. The RD Competition Notes does not specifically state that when panels 19 and 20 are illuminated in this way that drivers are to enter the pit lane. Car 16 (Maini) entered the pit entry road and then returned to the track after the bollard at SC1 in breach of ISC Apex L Ch IV (d) and in contravention to the Race Directors instructions. The driver explained that he did not have clear radio communication from his engineer until very late and it was to “follow safety car through pit lane”. He did not see a Safety Car. He understood that the arrow signal on light panel 20 meant that he was to stay to that side of the track and take an alternate route. Having no clear instruction on what to do and then seeing drivers behind him staying out on track he chose to return to the track after the bollard. While the driver failed to follow the intended instructions from the Race Director no driver benefited nor was harmed. When racing was resumed after the safety car period all drivers were in the correct positions with no advantage gained. Consequently the Stewards decide that while the regulations were breached the appropriate penalty in this case is a Warning to the driver given the late call and the lack of clarity surrounding the instructions.

documents.title: Doc 43 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - Gaining lasting advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - Gaining lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 20 (Fittipaldi) went off track while completing a pass on Car 4 (Herta) at Turns 11-12 thereby gaining lasting advantage.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 12.4.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Approaching Turn 11 Car 20 attempted an outside pass on Car 4, then went off track and rejoined at Turn 12 completing an overtake over Car 4. To have the rights for a turn the car who is trying to overtake on the outside has to have its front axle ahead of the front axle of the other car at the apex, and in this case Car 20 was not in this position. The Stewards considered that Car 20 went off track at the exit of Turn 11 and rejoined at Turn 12 gaining a position over Car 4. A successful overtake requires the driver to complete the manoeuvre on track. Having analysed extensively the matter, the Stewards, under these circumstances considered that failing to lose an advantage constitutes gaining an advantage. The stewards elect to impose the standard penalty for leaving the track and gaining a lasting advantage.

documents.title: Doc 26 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - Failure to follow RD instructions - chequered flag
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - Failure to follow RD instructions - chequered flag

details.fact: Car 20 (Fittipaldi) failed to follow the Race Director Competition Notes (document 4) instructions for returning to the Support Paddock pit lane after the end of the session.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code - in conjunction with Item 25.1 of the Race Director’s Competition Notes.
details.decision: Warning
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 15). The drivers were informed by the FIA Race Director during the Drivers Meeting that after taking the chequered flag they must continue and leave the track via the exit after Turn 10, to the F2 Paddock Parc Fermé. Car 9 was the first car to receive the chequered flag in the Practice session closely followed by Car 20. It is noteworthy that the last car not to have received the chequered flag was just in front of Cars 9 and 20. The Driver reported that he did not see the chequered flag at the line nor any yellow flag / light panel nor marshals on track signalling for him to turn into the support paddock, as they had expected. As a result he did not exit after Turn 10 and he continued on the track in breach of the RD instructions. The Stewards considered the mitigating circumstances that no yellow flag was shown nor light panel was illuminated and the facts of the configuration of this new circuit and the short time between the last car that had not seen the chequered flag and the first car that crossed the line after the session finished was very short and as such the marshals could not be on track and waving the flag. However, it is responsibility of the driver to follow the RD instructions and he did not. Therefore, in the light of the present case and given the mitigating circumstances mentioned above, the Stewards elect to give a warning to the driver.

details.fact: Car 23, Rafael Villagomez, did not comply with the requirement to reduce speed under single and double yellow flags at Turns 11 and 12 during the practice session.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A drop of 10 places on the grid for the Sprint and Feature races in which the driver participates. In addition, 3 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 3 points.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence and GPS evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representative (document 11). A yellow flag was shown at the entrance to turn 11 and then a double yellow entering turn 12 where there was a stopped car on the outside of the track on the exit. The driver of Car 23 reported that he was aware of both the yellow flag and the double yellow flag and he thought that he had lifted sufficiently. He then reported that after seeing that he was clear of the stopped car he resumed his push lap. The mini sector timing data revealed that the driver achieved his fastest time in both mini sectors up to that point in the session. There was no indication that the driver had lifted nor that he had abandoned his lap as is required when passing through a double yellow flag area. This is a violation of the regulations and relates to safety. The standard penalty of 10 grid drops is used as the Stewards could find no mitigating circumstances to vary the penalty. In keeping with Art 31.5 of the 2026 F2 Sporting Regulations the grid drop penalty will be applied to both the Sprint and Feature races.

documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 9 - failure to nominate both rear brake discs

details.infringement: Breach of Article 24.18 a of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A fine of 7000 Euros (being 2 x 3500 Euros) to be paid by the Competitor. details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 63) and heard the Team Representative. They examined the report (Document 62) from the Technical Delegate, who was also present at the Hearing at the request of the Stewards Panel. The Team did not dispute the Technical Delegate’s report that Car 9 used brake discs that were not properly nominated for the car as required by Article 24.18a) of the Formula 2 Sporting Regulations. The Team explained that this was an administrative error on their part. Stewards determined that Car 9 gained no Sporting Advantage during the race due to the error. The Stewards accept that administrative errors can occur but determine that an infringement exist nevertheless. Under the circumstances, the Stewards impose a fine of 7,000 Euro on the team and decide to reduce by two the number of brake disks available for the rest of the season (from 36 to 34 total) in accordance to Article 28.14. c) of the Formula 2 Sporting Regulations. The Stewards also mandate the team to declare the two discs used during the race (brake disc number: G5028 & G5029).

documents.title: Doc 59 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 3 - causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 3 - causing a collision

details.fact: Car 3 (Miyata) made contact with Car 10 (Goethe) at Turn 7.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 3 points
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 57 & 58) and heard the Drivers of Car 3 (Miyata) and Car 10 (Goethe) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence. The Driver of Car 10 explained that approaching Turn 7 he was clearly ahead of Car 3. When entering the corner, Car 3 stuck his front wing on the inside and made contact with the right rear tyre of Car 10. The Driver of Car 3 stated that he was ahead of Car 10 at Turn 6 and that he was squeezed by Car 10 in both the Turn 6 exit and the entry of Turn 7, which resulted in a contact between the two cars. Having considered the matter extensively, Stewards determined that Car 3 initiated an overtaking move on the inside of Car 10 at Turn 7. Video evidence showed that Car 3 made contact from his front axle to the right rear wheel of Car 10. Footage also confirmed that at no point was the front axle of Car 3 alongside the mirror of Car 10, as required in the 2026 Driving Standard Guidelines to have the right of the line when overtaking on the inside The Stewards determined that Car 3 was wholly to blame for the incident and imposed the baseline penalty of 10 seconds penalty plus two penalty points.

documents.title: Doc 46 - INFRINGEMENT - MP MOTORSPORT (Car 10) potentially unsafe act
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - MP MOTORSPORT (Car 10) potentially unsafe act

details.fact: A team member momentarily entered the Fast Lane to release Car 10.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code - potentially unsafe act.
details.decision: Reprimand to the Team.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 36) and heard the Team representative. They examined video evidence. During the qualifying session, a team member momentarily entered the fast lane to release Car 10. For safety reasons, it is essential that team members avoid crossing the white line separating the blending lane from the fast lane. This rule is crucial for maintaining safety and minimizing risks during high-pressure moments on the pit lane. The team manager explained that the limited space provided by the F1 Teams prevented them from having the necessary room to operate effectively. This was confirmed by the Race Director, who explained that a request would be made to improve this for all remaining sessions. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards concluded that, although the team did breach the regulations, there were mitigating circumstances. Specifically, the limited space available contributed to the situation, and the team member was only briefly in the fast lane. Taking these factors into account, the Stewards have decided to issue a reprimand to the team.

documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 2 - impeded Car 16 in Qualifying

details.fact: Car 2 (Duerksen) impeded Car 16 (Maini) at Turn 6 in Qualifying.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A drop of 3 places on the grid for the Sprint Race & Feature Race at this Competition. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 30 & 31) and heard the Drivers of Car 2 (Duerksen) and Car 16 (Maini) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence. Car 16 was on push lap and caught up to the back of Car 2 who was on a cool down lap, Car 16 was closing the gap quickly and at Turn 6 caught up with Car 2, who was on the racing line and impeded Car 16. Meanwhile, the driver of Car 16 claimed that he was on a push lap and was impeded by Car 2, who remained on the racing line. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 2 could have done more to avoid unnecessarily impeding on Car 16, consequently the Stewards apply the standard penalty of a drop 3 grid positions. documents.title: Doc 40 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - causing a collision

details.fact: Car 16 (Maini) made contact with Car 24 (Van Hoepen) at Turn 10 in Qualifying.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A drop of 3 places on the grid for the Sprint Race & Feature Race at this Competition. In addition, 1 point is to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 1 point
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 25 & 26) and heard the Drivers of Car 16 (Maini) and Car 24 (Van Hopene) and the team representatives. They examined the GPS information and video evidence. The driver of Car 24 explained that he was on a warm up lap. He also admitted being aware of Car 16 following closely and seeing a blue flag just before Turn 10. He stated that there was no space for Car 16 to overtake him at Turn 10 and he had no time to react to the blue flag as he was already turning for the corner. The driver of Car 16 confirmed that he was also on a warm up lap, but he wanted to get a better position on track and decided to first move to the right of the track and later to the left-hand side and start an overtaking move of Car 25. The Driver of Car 16 admitted making contact with the barriers before making contact with Car 24. Having considered the matter extensively, Stewards determined that Car 16 was too optimistic, trying to overtake Car 24, his front axle was alongside the rear wheel of Car 24 when the contact occurred. The Stewards noted the two blue flags displayed just before Turn 10 while both cars were in sequence at a similar speed and consider this a mitigating circumstance. The Stewards decided that Car 16 was predominantly to blame for the incident and elected to impose a drop of three grid positions for both races at this Competition plus 1 penalty point.

documents.title: Doc 72 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 22 - Out of position at first SC line
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 22 - Out of position at first SC line

details.fact: Car 22 (Varrone) failed to enter the pit lane after being out of position at the first safety car line.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 37.8 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Ten second Stop & Go Penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (d) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations, as specified in Article 37.8 of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement. The penalty, while not fully served during the Race, was nevertheless served to the satisfaction of the Stewards.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned and heard the driver and team representative (Document 56). They examined video and GPS evidence. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 22 was delayed leaving the grid and was passed by one car. Car 22 did not re-establish the original grid starting order before reaching Safety Car Line 1 and proceeded to start the race from his assigned grid position rather than entering the pits and starting from the end of the pit lane. The penalty specified by the regulation, a ten-second stop-and-go penalty was communicated by the stewards to Race Control. The message that was posted to the teams on Timing Page 3 said “Stop–And-Go”. Car 22 (VAR) entered the pit lane in due course came to a stop in its pit box and immediately departed without stopping for ten seconds. The stewards note that while a mere stop-and-go penalty is not among the listed penalties provided under Article 39.3, it is a penalty allowed by Article 12.4.1.l of the International Sporting Code. The team, having served the posted penalty, bears no fault in failing to serve the intended penalty. The stewards surmise that the confusion stems from the fact that the in the Formula 1 regulations, a stop-and-go penalty by definition includes an obligation to stop for ten seconds. Such is not the case within the F2 Sporting Regulations. Given the gap between the series regulations, it is imperative that penalty announcements in Formula 2 and 3 be made be made with clarity in these circumstances.

documents.title: Doc 68 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 12 - Driving unnecessarily slowly
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 12 - Driving unnecessarily slowly

details.fact: Car 12 (Boya), while contesting position with Car 11 (Montoya), drove unnecessarily slowly approaching the DRS detection zone triggering a collision between following cars.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.4 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 1 point to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 1 point.
details.reason: They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (Documents 61). The Stewards examined video and GPS evidence. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 12 (BOY) delayed in applying the throttle on the exit of Turn 10 because he did not want to be at a DRS disadvantage to Car 11 (MON) on the following straight. This was highly unpredictable to the following cars who applied the throttle normally and found themselves closing on BOY at a surprising rate. Car 22 (VAR), the first trailing car checked up, but Car 21 (SHI), the second car, did not have sufficient time or space to react and had nose to tail contact with VAR further causing VAR to collide with MON. The stewards determine that BOY drove unnecessarily slowly in a manner that proved to be dangerous to other cars and impose the baseline penalty for driving infractions. All drivers are reminded that predictability is one of the cornerstones of safety. The stewards note that the single penalty point imposed here is light for a corresponding 10 second penalty but feel that it is appropriate for this case of first impression. Future similar infractions may warrant increased points. While BOY received a penalty in this case, the stewards are pleased to note his exceptional candor and integrity during the hearing.

details.decision: Deletion of the fastest lap time set by Car 17 in the Qualifying Session. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 33). Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the Driver of Car 17 lost control of the car in Turn 4 and crashed resulting in a Red Flag and the session had to be stopped. documents.title: DOC 74 - 2026 Monza Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 2 - start set up procedure
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 2 - start set up procedure

details.fact: Car 2 (Durksen) did not engage the start set up procedure before coming to a halt after the Formation Lap.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 37.9 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Reprimand to the Driver of Car 2.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 71) and heard the Driver of Car 2 (Durksen) and the team representative. The Technical Delegate showed the data to the Stewards and the Driver and Team Representative. The driver of Car 2 explained that, at the end of the formation lap on the main straight, he was focused on building tyre temperature and ensuring that he stopped correctly within his grid box. He stated that he activated the start set-up procedure once the car had come to a stop in its designated grid position. The Team Representative explained that the race engineer had reminded the driver to activate the start set-up procedure when entering the grid. The Team also confirmed, based on its data, that the procedure had been activated prior to the start of the race. The Technical Delegate reported that Car 2 did not have the start set-up procedure activated before coming to a halt on the grid. However, the procedure was activated more than 30 seconds before the start signal was given. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the start set- up procedure was activated after the car had stopped on the grid, which constituted a breach of Article 37.9 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations . However, the procedure was activated well before the start of the race, thereby avoiding any potentially dangerous situation. Taking these mitigating circumstances into account, the Stewards elect to impose a Reprimand on the driver of Car 2.

documents.title: DOC 73 - 2026 Monza Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 8 - breach of RD instructions - tyre pit lane management
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 8 - breach of RD instructions - tyre pit lane management

details.fact: During the mandatory pit stop for Car 8 (Bilinski), the rear left tyre was rolled across the working area from one team member to another.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Warning given to the Competitor.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 57) and heard the team representatives. They examined video evidence. Following the pit stop of Car 8, the mechanic responsible for the left-rear tyre passed a tyre to his colleague on the right-rear side by rolling it across the pit stop box. The mechanic on the right-rear side caught the tyre and dropped it behind him, causing the tyre to momentarily rock in its position. The Team Representative acknowledged that the handling of the tyre could have been carried out in a better manner. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that, although the tyre only rocked momentarily and it did not roll when it was dropped by Car 8's mechanic, the tyre handling procedure was not carried out to the standard expected. On this occasion, the operation did not create an unsafe situation. However, passing tyres between mechanics by rolling them across the pit stop box has the potential to create a dangerous situation should the tyre not be caught correctly and instead rebound towards the fast lane. In light of the above, the Stewards elect to impose a Warning on the Team.

documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 12 - driving unnecessarily slowly

details.fact: Car 12 (Boya) was driving unnecessarily slowly off the racing line on the approach to Turn 11.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (e) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A drop of 3 places on the grid for the Sprint Race & Feature Race at this Competition. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 4 points
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 24) and heard the Driver of Car 12 (Boya) and the team representative. They examined video evidence. During the session, Car 12, which was leading a group of cars, slowed significantly on the exit of Turn 10 and began warming its tyres. The driver then moved to the right- hand side of the track, leaving the racing line clear to the left. Several cars approaching from behind elected to momentarily queue behind Car 12 rather than continue at normal speed on the racing line. The speed of Car 12 reduced to approximately 31 km/h. As additional cars caught the group, this resulted in two and, at times, three lines of cars travelling side by side at low speed, including on the racing line. The driver of Car 12 explained that he was leading a group of cars and chose to slow down in order to avoid providing a tow to the cars behind. He acknowledged that he reduced speed significantly, including selecting first gear, but stated that he was travelling off the racing line at all times. He further explained that he avoided accelerating and braking aggressively in order to avoid driving erratically. The Stewards acknowledge that there are occasions during practice and qualifying sessions when drivers may need to slow significantly off the racing line, or even come to a stop, in order to avoid impeding another car. Such circumstances may constitute driving "necessarily" slowly. In this case, however, the Stewards determined that Car 12 slowed to an excessively low speed without a valid sporting or safety justification. The sole purpose of this action was to seek a sporting advantage by avoiding providing a tow and potentially benefiting from one later in the lap. By doing so, Car 12 contributed to the formation of a queue of cars travelling at very low speed and to the circumstances that led to incidents involving multiple cars approaching Turn 11. Having carefully considered the matter, the Stewards conclude that Car 12 was driving unnecessarily slowly. Accordingly, they impose the standard penalty of a three grid place drop for both the Sprint Race and the Feature Race, together with two penalty points.

documents.title: DOC 36 - 2026 Monza Event - DECISION - Car 8 - alleged weaving in Qualifying
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 8 - alleged weaving in Qualifying

details.fact: Car 8 (Bilinski) was alleged to be weaving in a zone prohibited by the Race Director Competition Notes.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 23) and heard the Driver of Car 8 (Bilinski) and the team representative. They examined video evidence. The Driver of Car 8 explained that he was encountering a slow-moving queue of cars ahead, particularly after the second bridge following Turn 10, where the Race Director had specifically instructed drivers to maintain full pace and avoid travelling at slow speed on the racing line. The Driver of Car 8 further explained that he understood the Race Director’s instructions and therefore chose to overtake the queue. As there were cars running side-by-side ahead of him, he had to move further to the left, onto the racing line, in order to avoid this complex situation while maintaining full pace. In doing so, the Driver of Car 8 stated that he had to place two wheels on the edge of the track. After passing the queue and being ahead of the other cars before entering Turn 11, he subsequently weaved the car in order to remove dust and debris from the tyres, with the intention of having clean tyres for his final push lap of the session. He also admitted being aware that no other cars were close to him and that he was travelling at racing speed. Taking all the circumstances into consideration, the Stewards decided that No Further Action was appropriate.

documents.title: DOC 35 - 2026 Monza Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - driving in an erratic manner
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - driving in an erratic manner

details.fact: Car 6 (Tsolov) was weaving in an erratic manner, close to Car 11 (Montoya) on the approach to Turn 11.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (e) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A drop of 3 places on the grid for the Sprint Race & Feature Race at this Competition. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 6 points
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 29 & 27) and heard the Drivers of Car 6 (Tsolov) and Car 11 (Montoya) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence. The Driver of Car 11 explained that he saw Car 8 begin a flying lap and decided to follow him. He further stated that, as he approached Turn 11, he observed Car 6 warming its tyres on the racing line. To avoid a potential collision, he took avoiding action and left the track. The Driver of Car 6 explained that he was behind Car 12 and, after seeing several other cars begin their laps, decided to do the same. He stated that the cars ahead were attempting to create a gap before starting their laps, and he therefore began warming his tyres. He acknowledged that there were other cars behind but admitted that he did not expect Car 11 to be so close until he saw it alongside him. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 6 was driving erratically by warming its tyres on the racing line while not travelling at racing speed. As a result, Car 11 was forced to take avoiding action and leave the track. The Stewards therefore determined that Car 6 hindered Car 11 and elect to impose a three grid place penalty for both the Sprint Race and the Feature Race, together with two penalty points.

documents.title: Doc 27 - DECISION - Car 6 - allegedly yellow flag violation in Practice
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 6 - allegedly yellow flag violation in Practice

details.fact: Car 6 (Tsolov) was alleged to have breached yellow flag regulations.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 14) heard from the Driver of Car 6 (TSO), the team representatives and the FIA Technical Delegate. Together they reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video evidence, timing data and telemetry. During the hearing the driver stated that he was aware of the yellow flag and he lifted the throttle until he saw the green digi panel in front of him (at the exit of Turn 13). The Team provided telemetry evidence taken from the car which was verified with the Technical Delegate as being from the section of the track that was under single yellow at the time. The Stewards determined that the driver entered Turn 12, being the commencement of the yellow flag sector, at a higher speed to his previous and subsequent push laps as he was on an improving lap time. The telemetry confirmed that the driver made a discernible lift increasing from 5% to 20% while within the yellow flag sector, which was also reflected in his speed reduction between the entry to the apex of Turn 13 in comparison to the other push laps. This reduction in speed was higher than on any other push lap. Although the margin of compliance was minimal, the Stewards were satisfied that given the sequence of corners and the amount of the reduction in speed, the driver had reduced speed in response to the yellow flag. Having considered all of the available evidence, the Stewards determined that the driver complied with the requirements of the regulations and that no breach had occurred. Accordingly, no further action is taken. The Stewards emphasise that this decision is based on the specific facts of this case and should not be considered as setting a precedent for future cases.

documents.title: Doc 84 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - breach of non operational personnel regulations
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - breach of non operational personnel regulations

details.fact: Report received at 10:53 of a breach by non operational personnel associated with Campos in the Pit Lane during the Red Flag period.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 21.5 and Appendix 5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: - 20.000€ fine to be paid by the Competitor. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA - Disqualification of Car 5 from the Feature Race (Race 2). All cars originally classified behind Car 5 are moved up one place in the Race classification. All lap times set by Car 5 during the Race are cancelled. - Withdrawal of 25 championship points from the Team, Campos Racing. This penalty is applied with suspension of sentence subject to no further breach of the above mentioned article of the 2026 FIA F2 Sporting Regulations at any FIA F2 events during the remainder of the 2026 F2 Season..
details.reason: The Stewards examined the available evidence, summoned the Drivers and Team Manager (documents 69, 73 & 74). As the driver Noel LEON had already left the track, they only heard from Nikola TSOLOV and the Team Manager. A person declared as Non-Operational Personnel was observed wearing a radio headset fitted with a microphone, and therefore had the appearance of potentially being able to transit, and therefore not a “listen only headset”. This is alleged to be a breach of Appendix 5 and Article 21.5 of the F2 Sporting Regulations. Under the applicable regulations, Non-Operational Personnel may only be in possession of a listen-only radio headset. During the hearing, the Team Manager explained that the person concerned, who was a team guest, had inadvertently taken the wrong type of headset. The Stewards noted that the team guest had been approached by a Scrutineer and informed that the headset was not permitted as it was fitted with a microphone. The Scrutineer was advised in response that the microphone was folded upwards. Despite having been specifically advised that the headset was not permitted, the team guest subsequently put the headset back on and continued to use it. Nevertheless, the Team remains responsible for ensuring that radio equipment provided to Non-Operational Personnel and team guests complies with the applicable requirements. The regulations in this respect are clear: Non-Operational Personnel may only be in possession of a listen-only radio headset. The Team is expected to exercise greater care in controlling the allocation and use of such equipment. In determining the scope of the penalty, the Stewards also established that the team guest concerned was associated exclusively with Car 5 and had no involvement with the Team’s other car. The Stewards therefore considered that it would not be appropriate to apply the sporting consequence of this infringement to the other car and determined that the disqualification should apply only to Car 5. Furthermore, the team guest was observed using the non-compliant headset only during this session. There was no evidence before the Stewards that the guest had used the headset during any other session of the Competition. The Stewards therefore determined that the disqualification should be limited to Car 5 from the results of this session only. The Stewards emphasise that it remains the responsibility of the Team to ensure compliance with these requirements and to put appropriate measures in place to prevent any recurrence. Taking into account the circumstances above, the Stewards apply the above mentioned penalties.

documents.title: Doc 83 - DECISION - Car 17 - alleged unsafe release
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 17 - alleged unsafe release

details.fact: Alleged unsafe release from Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) when Car 15 (Dunne) was in the fast lane.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 28.12 (a) of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 67 & 68) and heard the Drivers of Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) and Car 15 (Dunne) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence. Car 15 entered the pit lane ahead of Car 17 both carrying out their mandatory pit stops. Car 15 was held in his pit position in order for another car to pass in the fast lane. This delay combined with perhaps a faster stop by car 17 resulted in Car 17 being released just after car 15 but in the pit position further ahead in the lane and hence ahead in position. When the driver of Car 17 was signalled to go, Car 15 was just leaving his pit area but was not yet in the fast lane. The Stewards used the other car in the fast lane as a reference point for the release of both Car 15 and 17 and concluded that each was released in a similar fashion relative to that car. Car 17 experienced some wheel spin when leaving his pit position and joined the fast lane immediately ahead of Car 15 but they were momentarily along side each other. The available space for Car 15 reduced as the two cars converged, and the driver of Car 15 elected to lift and fall behind Car 17. Car 17 was also seen to take avoiding action and briefly straddled the painted area in the pit lane separating the fast lane from the working lane. In judging if an unsafe release had occurred the Stewards assessed the circumstances at the point Car 17 completely cleared its pit-stop position, as required by Article 28.12 and also considered the point that the release signal was given to Car 17 and concluded that there was sufficient gap for the release to be done safely. The subsequent convergence between Cars 15 and 17 arose from simultaneous movement and Car 17’s wheelspin rather than an objectively unsafe gap at the release point. At all times both drivers were fully aware of each other and managed the situation appropriately. At the hearing the stewards were asked to consider whether either car had breached a regulation by driving along side each other briefly. Given the entire circumstances and how the drivers managed the situation the Stewards did not find that this reached to the level of a breach of the regulations either.

documents.title: Doc 77 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 9 - causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 9 - causing a collision

details.fact: Car 9 (Mini) made contact with Car 8 on Lap 1 at Turn 1.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Five seconds (5) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (a) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 1 point is to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 1 point.
details.reason: Having reviewed the available video evidence, the Stewards determined that Car 9 positioned itself on the right-hand side of the track approaching Turn 1. As the field approached Turn 1, Car 9 was squeezed towards the edge of the track, close to the grass, which compromised the driver’s approach in the braking area. At the apex of Turn 1, Car 9 attempted to overtake Car 8 on the inside. However, due to the lock-up and the resulting speed differential, Car 9 was unable to avoid contact with Car 8. The Stewards noted that the opening lap at Turn 1 of Spa-Francorchamps is a unique situation, with multiple cars negotiating a tight hairpin simultaneously and the available space reducing rapidly. Nevertheless, the Stewards determined that Car 8 had no realistic opportunity to avoid the collision, as it was constrained by another car to its left and was entitled to follow its chosen racing line through the corner. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards concluded that the driver of Car 9 was wholly responsible for the collision. While acknowledging the challenging circumstances of the opening lap at Turn 1, the Stewards determined that the driver of Car 9 failed to maintain sufficient control of the car under braking and was solely responsible for the resulting contact with Car 8. The Stewards therefore imposed a 5- second time penalty on the driver of Car 9.

documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 14 - Formation Lap - spacing not kept tight as possible

documents.title: Doc 60 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 7 - overtaking on the Formation Lap
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 7 - overtaking on the Formation Lap

details.fact: Car 7 (Beganovic) overtook Cars 14, 2 and 8 on the Formation Lap.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 37.8 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Warning given to the Driver of Car 7.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 52 and 53) and heard the Drivers of Car 7 (Beganovic) and Car 2 (Durksen) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence. During the Formation Lap, Cars 14, 8, 2 and 7 were travelling in sequence. Upon exiting Turn 17, Car 14 reduced its speed, which caused Cars 8 and 2 to slow accordingly. Car 7 was approaching at a higher speed and, upon realising that the cars ahead had slowed significantly, took evasive action by moving to the right-hand side of the track. In doing so, Car 7 left the track and overtook Cars 14, 8 and 2. Before entering Turn 18, Car 7 allowed all three cars to re-pass, thereby re- establishing its original starting order. During the hearing, the driver of Car 7 stated that he had been surprised by the speed of Car 14, which, in his view, was unusually slow at that point of the track. He explained that, upon realising the significant reduction in speed of the cars ahead, he took all reasonable measures to avoid a potential collision. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the driver of Car 7 should have been more aware of the speed at which the cars ahead were travelling. As a consequence of failing to do so, the driver was required to take evasive action to avoid a potential collision with Cars 8 and 2, leaving the track and overtaking multiple cars during the Formation Lap. The Stewards nevertheless accepted the driver’s explanation that the speed of Car 14 at the exit of Turn 17 was unusually slow for that section of the circuit. The Stewards concluded that, notwithstanding the circumstances described above, the driver of Car 7 remained responsible for controlling his speed and ensuring that he did not overtake other cars during the Formation Lap. Consequently, they decided to impose a warning to the driver of car 7.

documents.title: Doc 43 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - non respect of double waved yellow flags
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - non respect of double waved yellow flags

details.fact: Car 20 (Fittipaldi) failed to respect double waved yellow flags at Turn 19.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A drop of 10 places on the grid for the Sprint Race & Feature Race at this Competition. In addition, 3 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 3 points
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 30) and heard the Driver of Car 20 (Fittipaldi) and the team representatives. Together they examined the available video evidence, marshalling system data and timing and telemetry data. Car 20 entered the relevant sector while double yellow flags were being displayed. During the hearing, the driver stated that he saw the yellow flag and that he reduced his speed from T18 to the exit of T19. Despite this, the driver failed to react appropriately to the flag signals in the double yellow sector as it started after the exit of T19 to the control line. The telemetry data showed that Car 20 remained fully on throttle and did not make any meaningful reduction in speed in the sector. Furthermore, the driver set the fastest sector time while passing through the double yellow flag sector. Under double yellow flags, a driver must reduce speed significantly and must be prepared to change direction or stop. The Stewards find that the driver’s conduct failed to satisfy any of these requirements. Accordingly, the Stewards impose the above mentioned penalty.

documents.title: Doc 42 - DECISION - Car 2 - alleged non respect of double waved yellow flags
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 2 - alleged non respect of double waved yellow flags

details.fact: Car 2 (Durksen) was alleged to have failed to respect double waved yellow flags at Turn 19.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 28) and heard the Driver of Car 2 (Durksen) and the team representatives. Together they examined the available video evidence, marshalling system data and timing and telemetry data. The sector under evaluation was the last sector of the track starting at the exit of Turn 19 and ending at the Control line. In comparing the sector times it is relevant to understand that the ideal line for the start of a push lap yields a faster sector time than is achieved when the sector is the last one of a push lap. This is because the drivers are able to make a different exit from Turn 19 when not following the T18 to T19 sequence. As a result an initial view of the sector times gave the impression that the driver may not have respected the double yellow requirements. Looking at the detailed telemetry data showed that the driver had lifted significantly and went back to throttle later in reaction to the double yellow. So although the sector time may not have shown an increase in time the drivers reaction did reflect the appropriate action. Accordingly the Stewards concluded that the driver did respect the requirements in this particular case.

documents.title: Doc 36 - DECISION - Car 17 - alleged non respect of double waved yellow flags

details.fact: Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) was alleged to have failed to respect double waved yellow flags at Turn 19.

details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 26) and heard the Driver of Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) and the team representatives. documents.title: Doc 35 - DECISION - Car 24 - allegedly the sole cause of the issuance of the red flag
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 24 - allegedly the sole cause of the issuance of the red flag

details.fact: Car 24 (Van Hoepen) was allegedly the sole cause of the issuance of the red flag.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 33.5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 24) and heard the Driver of Car 24 (Van Hoepen) and the team representative. Car 24 stopped on the circuit after suffering a gearbox failure, which resulted in the session being red flagged. The FIA Technical Delegate confirmed through the recorded data that the gearbox malfunction prevented the driver from selecting gears and that the failure was caused by a genuine technical failure. Having considered the matter extensively and having consulted with the FIA Technical Delegate, the Stewards determined that, whilst Car 24 was the immediate cause of the red flag, the driver could not be regarded as the sole cause of the red flag within the meaning of Article 33.5 of the Sporting Regulations. Article 33.5 provides the Stewards with the discretion to determine whether the deletion of the driver's fastest qualifying lap is warranted where a driver is the sole cause of a red flag. The purpose of the Article is to address situations in which a driver's actions have unfairly compromised the qualifying attempts of other competitors. In the present case, the evidence establishes that the red flag resulted from an unforeseen mechanical failure outside the driver's control. The driver neither contributed to nor could reasonably have avoided the incident. Accordingly, the Stewards find that the circumstances do not justify the deletion of the driver's fastest qualifying lap.

documents.title: Doc 34 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - sole cause of the issuance of the red flag
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - sole cause of the issuance of the red flag

details.fact: Car 5 (Leon) was the sole cause of the issuance of the red flag.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 33.5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Car 5 is determined to have been the sole cause of the Red Flag issued at 16:00 hours Deletion of all lap times set during the Qualifying Session after the Red Flag which was issued at 16:00 hours No lap time was set prior to the Red Flag, so the Stewards were unable to delete the fastest lap set prior to the Red Flag Start permission given for both Races, to be placed on the grid in accordance with Article 34.2 of the F2 Sporting Regulations
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 23) and heard the Driver of Car 5 (Leon) and the team representative. They reviewed video evidence and determined that, at the start of the Qualifying Session, Car 5 was on its out-lap. While negotiating the apex of Turn 4, Car 5 lost control, spun and came to a stop on the left-hand side of the track at the exit of Turn 4. A red flag was subsequently declared by the Race Director. Car 5 was then able to restart the car without assistance and followed the red flag procedure, proceeding directly to the Pit Lane. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards noted that the track had been declared wet by the Race Director prior to the commencement of the session. The Driver of Car 5 was therefore aware of the prevailing track conditions when entering Turn 4. Having reviewed the available evidence, the Stewards determined that no external factors contributed to the spin and that the incident was solely caused by the Driver of Car 5. Consequently, the Driver of Car 5 was determined to be solely responsible for the incident which resulted in the red flag. During the hearing, the Team Representative indicated that he had sought permission from the Race Director for the Driver to continue. As the incident had not yet been investigated by the Stewards and no decision on the Sole Cause of the Red Flag had been determined, the Race Director properly responded that the Driver could continue. It has been agreed with the teams that the Sole Cause of a Red Flag will be investigated after a session when it is not absolutely clear to the Stewards that there was no mechanical or other cause outside the control of the Driver. Considering the unique sequence of events in this case, the Stewards determined that they would not immediately hold the driver responsible and hence permitted him to continue. It was the driver's choice to continue in the session, knowing that all times set thereafter may have been invalidated. The Stewards, therefore, decided to invalidate all lap times set by Car 5 after the red flag was issued. No lap time was set prior to the Red Flag, so the Stewards were unable to delete the fastest lap set prior to the Red Flag. Car 5 therefore has no valid lap time recorded during the qualifying session. Finally, considering that car 5 set a suitable lap time within the 107% limit during free practice session, the Stewards permit Car 5 to start both Races behind all the classified drivers.
